note: Agents MUST load the listed module before writing each surface (APPLY, not prefer). HSW is the default for EVERY human-facing deliverable except README/product entry (writing-direction) and filename-only surfaces (human-output-naming). No per-report or per-HTML opt-in. Soft = no NLP CI grade of prose; presence of modules + this contract (including always-on inject) is what validate_content_system and verify_hsw_applied check. EVERY CGM adopter must inject the always-on system_block into agent prompts at start (see acs_prompt_inject / always_on_system_block). Filename surfaces route to human-output-naming (hon) with speakable basenames + per-feature legends; see also docs/human-output-naming.json / docs/HUMAN_OUTPUT_NAMING.md.

routes.notes: Keep scan-first selective bold and the README scanability contract.

Reader-facing product/research explanations (plans, architecture writeups, evidence briefs) route to writing-direction: story order, scan-first selective bold, evidence/status/boundaries distinct, clear next action. This is NOT manuscript/data-writeup prose — a scholarly paper or raw data writeup routes to human-sounding-writing (hsw) instead. Do not copy the README outline mechanically onto a brief; adapt the checks to the document type.
review_checklist: Story order: name the recognizable human situation, then the concrete problem and consequence, before mechanism or architecture.
Connect each important paragraph to why it matters and to an evidence, example, or boundary — not to style alone.
Keep evidence, status, and boundaries distinct: say what a cited source supports, what it leaves unproven, and the inspected revision.
Use descriptive headings and selective bold so a heading-and-bold scan tells a usable second story; do not turn the brief into a README clone.
End with a clear next action, example, or smallest useful path for the reader.
Adapt the checks to the document type; do not add promotional claims a research brief does not support.

routes.notes: Human voice, AI-tell scrub, restrained bold. Includes chart/takeaway guidance for papers and data writeups. Commit messages and commit subjects are in scope — MUST load hsw before writing them. HTML reports, compare HTML/UIs, appendable HTML, and other agent-produced human-readable HTML are in scope — MUST load hsw by default; no per-report opt-in. Filename basenames stay on human-output-naming (hon). Receipts (push, checkpoint, release) are human-facing prose and route here too; the title and reference rules are in docs/NARRATIVE_AUTHORITY.md.

title_contract.rule: A title is one complete, understandable human sentence stating what is wrong or what the reader gets. No leading prefix codes (feat:, fix:, chore:, docs:, refactor:, test:, ci:, build:, perf:, style:, revert:) and no internal task numbers (#45, CGM-0045, TASK-0045, M5) as the first token.
title_contract.reference_rule: Give every commit SHA, pull request number, flag, or file path a plain-English meaning in the same sentence before it carries weight.
checklist: Read the title alone: does it state what is wrong or what the reader gets?
Strip any leading prefix code or internal task number; the title must still read as one human sentence.
Name what each SHA, pull request number, flag, or file path is before it does any work.
No colon-reveal slogan; the title is a sentence, not a label with a subtitle.

routes.notes: Filesystem names for generated media and manifest paths. Default speakable basenames (identity first; omit defaults); optional style=safe_twin. Reject hashy junk and robot key=value stems. Keep a per-feature filename legend (glossary + file list). See docs/HUMAN_OUTPUT_NAMING.md.

apply_checklist: Identify the writing surface (README, product entry, human-facing research plan / architecture explanation / evidence brief, PR title/body, issue title/body, issue-log title, commit message/subject, non-README doc, changelog prose, post/blog/social, paper/data writeup, HTML report, compare HTML/UI, or other human-facing HTML/artifact).

Look up the surface in routes[].surfaces in docs/writing-routing.json (or the table in docs/WRITING_ROUTING.md). If it is a reader-facing research plan, architecture explanation, or evidence brief, route to writing-direction (see the reader_facing_explanations route and its review_checklist) — a scholarly paper or raw data writeup still routes to human-sounding-writing (hsw). If it is human-facing and not README/product entry, not a reader-facing explanation, and not a filename-only surface, default to human-sounding-writing (human_facing_default).
MUST load modules/<load>/SKILL.md for that route before drafting — required_load is true; do not skip because the surface is short, 'just a commit', or 'just an HTML report'.
Apply the module rules to the draft (voice, AI-tell scrub, bold policy as the module states).
README / product entry stays on writing-direction; do not apply hsw bold restraints there.

Human-facing research plans, architecture explanations, and evidence briefs route to writing-direction (reader_facing_explanations); apply its review_checklist. A scholarly paper or raw data writeup still routes to hsw.

If the surface is a generated artifact filename, asset-manifest path, committed media basename, or filename legend, MUST load modules/human-output-naming/SKILL.md (hon), call scripts/human_filename (speakable by default; optional safe_twin), and keep a per-feature legend.
Never treat HSW as optional, soft-skip, or per-report opt-in for human-facing HTML, compare UIs, or agent-produced readable artifacts.

acs_prompt_inject.when: At agent start / session boot for EVERY repo that pins CGM — not per-report and not ACS-only. Paste system_block into the agent system prompt before the agent writes ANY human-facing deliverable: GitHub or docs prose, HTML reports, compare HTML/UIs, appendable HTML, posts, papers, or other agent-produced human-readable artifacts — and before naming generated artifact / asset-manifest / media paths.
acs_prompt_inject.system_block:
CGM ALWAYS-ON WRITING RULE (every adopter that pins this helper)

Before you write ANY human-facing output — including HTML reports, compare HTML/UIs, appendable HTML, PR/issue/commit prose, docs, posts, papers, or other readable artifacts — you MUST load and apply modules/human-sounding-writing/SKILL.md (hsw).

This rule is always on. Opt-in is forbidden. Do not wait for a per-task, per-report, or per-HTML flag.

Exceptions (only these):
- README.md / product entry pages → load modules/writing-direction/SKILL.md instead
- Human-facing research plans, architecture explanations, and evidence briefs → load modules/writing-direction/SKILL.md (reader-facing explanation, not a manuscript or data writeup)
- Generated artifact filenames / asset-manifest paths / media basenames / filename legends → load modules/human-output-naming/SKILL.md (hon) for basenames; visible prose inside HTML still uses hsw

HTML reports, compare HTML, and compare UIs have NO skip path. An exception reason is not allowed for those surfaces.

If you cannot load the skill file from the pinned CGM checkout, stop and report that — do not draft jargon-heavy or tool-dump HTML instead.

Filenames: use scripts/human_filename (speakable basenames; optional safe_twin) and keep a per-feature legend. Hash may stay a separate manifest field.
acs_prompt_inject.instruction: ALWAYS-ON for every CGM adopter (ACS is one consumer, not the only one). Paste acs_prompt_inject.system_block into the agent system prompt at start. HSW (human-sounding-writing) is ON by default for EVERY human-facing task/output. Before writing ANY human-facing output (including HTML/compare), MUST load modules/human-sounding-writing/SKILL.md. Opt-in is forbidden; always_on is true. Skipping requires an explicit machine-readable exception reason that is NOT allowed for HTML reports, compare HTML, or compare UIs. README and product entry pages → writing-direction. Human-facing research plans, architecture explanations, and evidence briefs → writing-direction (reader_facing_explanations; a scholarly paper or raw data writeup stays on hsw). Pull request titles/bodies, issue titles/bodies, issue-log titles, commit messages, commit subjects, non-README docs, changelog prose, posts/blogs/social/general prose, papers/data writeups, HTML reports, compare HTML, compare UIs, appendable HTML reports, and other agent-produced human-readable HTML → human-sounding-writing (hsw). Soft enforcement means no NLP CI grade of prose; the contract language is MUST/APPLY/default_on/always_on, not prefer. Follow apply_checklist and human_facing_default in this file. Generated artifact filenames, asset-manifest paths, committed media basenames, and filename legends → human-output-naming (hon): MUST load that skill and use scripts/human_filename with speakable basenames (omit defaults; optional safe_twin); keep a per-feature legend (glossary + file list); never opaque p0/hex stems or robot key=value stems. Prose and visible text inside HTML still use hsw; basenames use hon.

human_facing_default.notes: Default ON for all human-facing deliverables. Do not treat HSW as optional, per-report, or only-when-writing-posts. README/product entry stays on writing-direction; reader-facing research plans, architecture explanations, and evidence briefs also stay on writing-direction (reader_facing_explanations route); basename/legend naming stays on human-output-naming (hon). Prose and visible text inside HTML reports and compare UIs still use HSW.

always_on_system_block.notes: Canonical paste text lives at acs_prompt_inject.system_block (name kept for pin compatibility). Every CGM adopter must inject it at agent start.

bootstrap_steps: At session start, read .content-system/ and the pinned CGM checkout; do not read the helper's moving main.
Paste acs_prompt_inject.system_block into the agent system prompt before writing any human-facing deliverable; opt-in is forbidden.

MUST load modules/writing-direction/SKILL.md for README/product entry, modules/human-sounding-writing/SKILL.md for PR/issue/commit prose, docs, and HTML reports, and modules/human-output-naming/SKILL.md for generated filenames and legends.
Generate the full narrative image set (hero PNG raster, problem, supporting) and register each in .content-system/asset-manifest.json with a prompt record; never use an SVG as the README hero.
Before handoff, run validate_content_system.py --check-adopter-readme (or verify_adopter_content.py) and fix failures.
antigravity.notes: Google Antigravity reads .content-system but did not proactively load the deep writing guidance (issue #35). This entry points the agent at the always-on system block and the full-depth README requirements. See docs/ANTIGRAVITY_INTEGRATION.md.
